# SDLC-FR-0101 — Accept authenticated event submissions

## Requirement

The service must accept event submissions only from callers that present a valid service token, and reject every other submission.

## Detailed Behavior

A submission carries an event type, a source identifier and a JSON payload of at most 64 KB. A missing, expired or unknown token is rejected with an explicit authentication error and nothing is stored.

## Rationale

Only known internal producers may write events.

## Acceptance / Verification

A submission without a valid token is rejected and leaves no stored record; a valid one is acknowledged with an event id.

## Constraints & Edge Cases

Payloads above 64 KB are rejected as too large.

## Non-Goals

Does not define how service tokens are issued.

## Open Questions

None.

--- Requirement SDLC-FR-0102 (entity synthetic-102, tree fingerprint e0336aa1e7b26d5e996c26158407772e72bc988dca98e81d4b371b9ec94f233a) ---

# SDLC-FR-0102 — Validate and persist accepted events

## Requirement

Every accepted event must be validated against its event type's schema and persisted durably before it is acknowledged.

## Detailed Behavior

An event that fails validation is rejected with the validation errors and is not persisted. A persisted event keeps its submission time, source identifier and payload unchanged.

## Rationale

Consumers rely on stored events being valid and complete.

## Acceptance / Verification

An acknowledged event can be read back unchanged after a service restart; an invalid event is never stored.

## Constraints & Edge Cases

Event type schemas are versioned; an unknown event type is rejected.

## Non-Goals

Does not define the event type schemas themselves.

## Open Questions

None.

# SDLC-FR-0103 — Report event processing status

## Requirement

A caller must be able to retrieve the processing status of a submitted event by its event id, and every failure must be visible in an audit log.

## Detailed Behavior

Status retrieval returns exactly one of RECEIVED, STORED or REJECTED for a known event id and a not-found result for an unknown one; the same id always returns the same status once it is final. Errors are bounded: no request waits longer than five seconds, and every rejection or internal error writes one audit entry.

## Rationale

Producers need a deterministic way to confirm what happened.

## Acceptance / Verification

Repeated status reads of a final event return the same value; every rejection appears once in the audit log.

## Constraints & Edge Cases

Audit entries never contain the event payload.

## Non-Goals

Does not define an audit retention period.

## Open Questions

None.
